paper_evaluations.title: Massage for rehabilitation after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

1.reason: Title explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

2.reason: Abstract lacks several PRISMA 2020 Abstracts elements (e.g., registration, funding, certainty, full eligibility details).

3.reason: Background places the review in context of KOA, TKA complications, massage evidence gaps, and absence of prior SRs.

4.reason: Explicit objective stated: evaluate effectiveness of massage for postoperative TKA rehabilitation.

5.reason: PICOS inclusion/exclusion criteria specified; studies grouped by outcomes and time points for synthesis.

6.reason: Five databases named and searched from inception to May 2024.

7.reason: Full search strategies not presented in the paper; only example terms and a supplement citation.

8.reason: Two independent reviewers screened titles/abstracts then full texts; disagreements resolved by discussion or third reviewer.

9.reason: Two independent reviewers extracted data; disagreements resolved by discussion or third party.

10a.reason: Outcomes listed but no statement whether all compatible results (measures, time points, analyses) were sought or selection methods.

10b.reason: Some study characteristics listed; assumptions about missing/unclear data not described.

11.reason: Cochrane RoB tool named but number of reviewers and independence for RoB assessment not specified.

12.reason: MD or SMD with 95% CI specified for continuous outcomes.

13a.reason: No description of processes (e.g., tabulation against planned groups) to decide eligibility for each synthesis.

13b.reason: No methods described for handling missing summary statistics or data conversions.

13c.reason: Forest plots and a characteristics table used to display individual and pooled results.

13d.reason: Random/fixed-effects models based on I2, Q statistic, RevMan 5.3 and Stata 16.0, with rationale given.

13e.reason: Subgroup analysis by country used to explore heterogeneity for length of stay.

13f.reason: Authors state sensitivity analyses were not performed because of the small number of studies per outcome.

14.reason: Begg’s and Egger’s tests described to assess publication/reporting bias.

15.reason: No methods (e.g., GRADE) described to assess certainty of evidence.

16a.reason: Search-to-inclusion numbers reported and a flow diagram (Fig. 1) provided.

16b.reason: Exclusion reasons given numerically but excluded studies that might have met criteria are not cited.

17.reason: All 11 included studies cited and characteristics presented in Table 1.

18.reason: Risk-of-bias assessments presented in Fig. 2 and summarized in text.

19.reason: Forest plots present effect estimates, CIs, and study-level data for the reported outcomes.

20a.reason: No brief summary of characteristics and risk of bias among studies contributing to each synthesis.

20b.reason: Pooled MD/SMD, 95% CIs, I2 and p-values presented for each meta-analysis.

20c.reason: Subgroup results by country for length of stay are presented.

20d.reason: No sensitivity-analysis results presented (none were conducted).

21.reason: Egger/Begg results and notes on infeasible tests for small outcomes are reported.

22.reason: No certainty (GRADE or equivalent) assessments presented for any outcome.

23a.reason: Results interpreted in light of pain mechanisms, muscle recovery, DVT literature and prior work.

23b.reason: Limitations of included evidence (China-centric, low-moderate quality, high heterogeneity) discussed.

23c.reason: Review-process limits (possible missed grey literature, no sensitivity analyses, blinding difficulties) discussed.

23d.reason: Implications for adjunctive practice and need for larger, higher-quality, multicenter trials stated.

24b.reason: Protocol registered in PROSPERO, indicating where it can be accessed.

24c.reason: No description or explanation of any amendments to the registration/protocol.

25.reason: Funding stated as not applicable; no other support or funder role described.

26.reason: Authors declare they have no competing interests.

27.reason: Data available on request only; templates, extracted data, analytic code and other materials not reported as publicly available.

item_1.reason: The title explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

item_3.reason: Only inclusion of RCTs of massage after TKA is stated; exclusion criteria are not specified.

item_4.reason: Five databases are named and last searched from inception to May 2024.

item_5.reason: The Cochrane Risk of Bias Assessment Tool is named as the RoB method.

item_6.reason: The abstract states a meta-analysis of specified outcomes was performed.

item_7.reason: Eleven RCTs and 940 participants are given, but study characteristics are not summarised.

item_8.reason: Direction of effects is described, but no summary estimates, CIs, or n per outcome are reported.

item_9.reason: Large heterogeneity of the included studies is briefly noted as a limitation.

item_10.reason: Results are interpreted as supporting massage as adjunctive post-TKA rehabilitation.

item_11.reason: No funding source is reported in the abstract.

item_12.reason: No register name or registration number is provided.
